spatial_claims.claim: A is a point outside the circle; secant from A meets circle at B (convex circumference) then C; D is on the circumference
AT is tangent from A touching circle at T; O is the center of the circle
AT² = AD² (hence AT = AD) derived from 3.36 applied to secant AC and tangent AT, combined with hypothesis AC·AB = AD²
OT = OD as radii; angle OTA = 90° (tangent perpendicular to radius by 3.18)
OA² = OT² + AT² by Pythagorean theorem (1.47) on right triangle OTA
OA² = OD² + AD² by substitution of equal quantities
O, A, D are not collinear — triangle OAD exists
Angle ODA = 90° by converse Pythagorean (1.48) in triangle OAD
DO produced through O is a diameter ending at D
AD is perpendicular to the diameter at endpoint D, so AD falls outside the circle (3.16) and is tangent at D

configuration_map: A is outside the circle throughout. B and C lie on the circle along the secant from A (B nearer to A on convex side). D is on the circumference; AD is the line to be proved tangent. T is an auxiliary tangent point on the circumference (from 3.17). O is the center. Key relationships: OT = OD (radii), AT = AD (from equal squares via 3.36 and hypothesis), angle OTA = 90° (tangent-radius perpendicularity), triangle OAD exists (non-collinearity proved by contradiction using 2.4), angle ODA = 90° (converse Pythagorean 1.48). The diameter through D and O is perpendicular to AD at D, placing AD outside the circle (3.16), confirming tangency.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof constructs an auxiliary tangent AT, uses 3.36 to establish AT = AD, applies the Pythagorean theorem (1.47) on right triangle OTA, substitutes equal quantities to get OA² = OD² + AD², proves non-collinearity of O-A-D, then applies the converse Pythagorean (1.48) to conclude angle ODA = 90°. Every spatial claim follows validly from the established configuration. The approach differs from Heath (who uses I.8 triangle congruence) but introduces no configuration contradictions.
